evidence: The user's hash has a typo — actual HEAD is 87973416c25d70f0f3c65f8147ae3a321fce55dd. Findings No blocking issues. This is a minimal, well-targeted fix. Core fix is correct (MapPopup.ts:2721): changing loading="lazy" to loading="eager" on the data-faa-camera-image . I verified experimentally: reverting to lazy and rerunning the new Playwright test causes it to hang past timeout rather than fail cleanly — confirming the deadlock is real. A hidden image is not "near the viewport," so Chromium's lazy-loading heuristic defers the load indefinitely; nothing ever un-hides it to trigger the load, since image.hidden = false only happens inside the load handler (MapPopup.ts:2762) — a genuine circular dependency, not just a cosmetic flicker. Resolver/race logic is untouched — this commit doesn't touch resolveFrameUrl, the abort-controller lifecycle, or the popup-replacement guards from the parent commit; those were already reviewed and are unaffected here. Unit test addition (map-popup-faa-camera.test.mts:74) is a correct, cheap invariant check (image.loading === 'eager') — good regression guard against someone reintroducing lazy on this element. E2e test (webcam-navigation.spec.ts:160-212) — I ran it directly against real Chromium and it passes (7.4s) with the fix in place. It correctly exercises the full path: sidecar JSON resolve → real decode → visibility → status span removal, using an actual 1×1 PNG so naturalWidth is a real assertion, not a mock. Good test. Residual risk (non-blocking, worth flagging) e2e/webcam-navigation.spec.ts is not wired into any CI workflow. I checked every .github/workflows/*.yml: only e2e/variant-identity.spec.ts (variant-e2e.yml) and e2e/a11y-baseline.spec.ts (accessibility.yml) run in CI. npm run test:e2e:full, which would run this whole spec file including the new test, isn't invoked anywhere in CI. This is a pre-existing gap (not introduced by this commit — the file already existed and wasn't CI-wired before), but it means the regression protection this commit adds only fires when someone remembers to run test:e2e:full locally.
